title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: KMP
tiers.description: Key Management Personnel, comprising the Directors, Officers and Senior Executives of the Company. The Policy applies only to their own 'private dealings' in Whitefield's issued securities; it does not extend its dealing prohibitions to associates, though a KMP must not procure another person to deal on their behalf while they are themselves prohibited from dealing.

windows.start_anchor: end of a financial reporting period (half-year or full year)
windows.end_anchor: day after the preliminary announcement of the half-yearly or annual results
day after the release of the monthly Net Asset Backing Announcement

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may from time to time designate a period of time as a prohibited period under this Policy; the Policy does not state whether such designations are made public or kept confidential.

rules.detail: No definition of 'Dealing' or 'Securities' is given anywhere in the Policy. Derivatives, options or other financial products referencing WHI securities are not named, and it is unclear whether the general 'deal in the Company's securities' prohibitions extend to them.
No hedging provision of any kind.
Outright, unconditional ban on short selling of the Company's securities by KMP.
rules.evidence: KMPs must not engage in short selling of the Company's securities

rules.detail: Granting security over Company securities is not mentioned.
Secured financing generally is not mentioned.
No holding-period or short-term trading rule beyond the specific ban on short selling (2.3).

clearance.approver: Most senior available executive director (other than one involved in the transaction), who must refer the matter to the most senior independent director (other than one involved in the transaction)
clearance.evidence: Approval may only be provided to such a request where both the executive and independent directors (a) consider there to be a sufficiently exceptional circumstance that the implementation of the general Policy would produce an inappropriate outcome, and (b) only if the KMP has confirmed that they are not in possession of any price sensitive information that has not been disclosed to market.

exceptions.evidence: Transfers of securities where there is no change in relevant interest
An investment in an entity where the assets of the entity are invested at the discretion of a third party
Responding to a corporate action or offer which has been made to all the Company's security holders of the same class
Transactions conducted between a KMP and a close family member
Transactions which are outside the control of the KMP, including those which result from the application of law.

exemption_authority: The most senior available executive director (other than one involved in the transaction) refers a written application to the most senior independent director (other than one involved); both must agree there is a sufficiently exceptional circumstance and that the KMP holds no undisclosed price sensitive information before approval is given in writing specifying the scope and timing of the transaction (Section 5).

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to private dealings in Whitefield's issued securities by Key Management Personnel (KMP).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy never defines 'Dealing' or 'Securities' and contains no attachment on either, so whether an OTC put/call, a hedge, or a secured loan over WHI shares is caught by the closed-period or UPSI prohibitions at all is genuinely unclear and would fall back on general Corporations Act insider trading concepts rather than this Policy's own text.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMPs must not deal in the Company's securities during prohibited periods (closed periods) unless exceptional circumstances apply and written approval is given to a transaction in advance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside a closed period and absent price sensitive information, the Policy imposes no notification or preclearance requirement at all on ordinary dealing, so a collar entered in an open window would not need any sign-off under this Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP's must not procure another person to deal in the Company's securities where they themselves are prohibited from dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A KMP cannot direct the bank (or anyone else) to execute a collar leg on their behalf during a period when the KMP is personally prohibited from dealing, even if the bank is acting as principal counterparty.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Transactions which are outside the control of the KMP, including those which result from the application of law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This exclusion from Section 2 (the UPSI and closed-period bans) is broad enough to arguably cover a secured lender's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default, since that sale is outside the KMP's control, though the Policy does not use lender or security-specific language so this reading is not certain.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Transactions conducted between a KMP and a close family member ... The following circumstances are excluded from the application of Section 2 of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: On its face this excludes transactions between a KMP and a close family member from all of Section 2, including the UPSI-possession ban, which is an unusually broad carve-out; routing collar-related transfers through a family member should still be treated cautiously given the underlying insider trading law is unaffected.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP's are not permitted to trade in the Company's Securities during the period from the end of a calendar month until the day after the release of the monthly Net Asset Backing Announcement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a listed investment company, WHI has a monthly closed period on top of the half-year/annual one, materially narrowing the windows available each year for collar entry, roll or unwind.

summary: A funded collar over vested WHI shares faces little express restriction, but also little express permission, because the Policy never defines 'Dealing' or 'Securities' and says nothing about derivatives, hedging, margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing. Outside the half-yearly/annual and monthly closed periods, and absent undisclosed price sensitive information, ordinary dealing by KMP requires no notification or clearance under this Policy, which would make entering a collar and its secured loan straightforward if it is not otherwise caught by general insider trading law. Dealing during a closed period is only possible with written approval from the most senior available executive and independent directors on an exceptional-circumstances basis, confirming the KMP holds no undisclosed price sensitive information. Short selling is expressly and unconditionally banned, and a KMP cannot procure a third party (such as the bank) to deal on their behalf while personally prohibited. The exclusion for 'transactions outside the control of the KMP' may protect a secured lender's enforcement sale from the closed-period ban, but this is an inference rather than an express carve-out, so bespoke legal advice on characterisation is needed before relying on it.
